repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owns the column model, schema-discovery consumer, REST API and metadata.dataset.changed.v1 publisher, so it must store per-column classification, suggest it from ingested tags, expose a steward override endpoint, return it in column metadata and change events, and stop re-ingestion from wiping it.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Holds the spec of record for the metadata-graph OpenAPI and the event schemas, which need additive classification/tag fields, the new override endpoint and the masked-columns field in access decisions.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: REST clients must use its MetadataClient, so it needs the classification fields on column metadata and a method to set/override a column classification.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Produces ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, whose column entries today carry only name/type/nullable, so it must parse source column comments such as `tags: pii,email` and emit them as an additive per-column tags field.

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and is the natural owner of access decisions, so it must read column classifications and return the columns to mask when the requester lacks a pii:read grant.

repositories.name: query-service
repositories.reason: Whatever service returns query results to data consumers (not present in the workspace) must apply the masked_columns from the access decision to result values.

repositories.name: dq-service
repositories.reason: Publishes dq.result.published.v1 and runs data-quality checks, so it must look up column classifications and apply PII-format validation rules to PII columns.

repositories.name: reporting-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1, which gains additive column fields, so its consumer must be re-tested for tolerant parsing (code change only if it also serves column values to consumers, see open questions).

considered_not_impacted.name: graph database (infrastructure behind GRAPH_DB_URL)
considered_not_impacted.reason: Classification is stored as extra properties on existing column nodes, which needs a metadata-graph store change but no separate repository or engine change, assuming the graph DB is schemaless for node properties.

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].tags (array of lowercase strings parsed from the source column comment, e.g. `tags: pii,email` -> ["pii","email"]) and optional columns[].comment; absent means no tags.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional columns[].classification (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII or null), columns[].classification_source (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) and columns[].tags; classification overrides are published with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED so no new enum value is introduced.

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column object gains classification, classification_source, suggested_classification and tags; existing fields are unchanged.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: Steward sets or overrides a column classification with body {classification, reason}; returns the updated column, 400 on invalid value, 404 on unknown dataset/column, 403 without steward permission, and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (COLUMNS_CHANGED).

contracts.name: POST /v1/access/decisions
contracts.description: Access decision response gains masked_columns (list of column names classified PII when the requester has no pii:read grant; empty list otherwise); endpoint path is inferred because entitlements-service is not in the workspace.

contracts.name: POST /v1/queries
contracts.description: Result values in masked columns are replaced with a type-compatible masked value and the response gains optional masked_columns metadata; endpoint path is inferred because the query service is not in the workspace.

open_questions: Only metadata-graph is present in the workspace; which repositories actually exist for the ingestion service, the DQ service and the query path that returns data to consumers (names ingestion-service, dq-service and query-service are inferred)?
Does reporting-service only consume metadata, or does it also return column values to consumers (in which case it needs masking too and becomes code_change)?
Is entitlements-service the owner of access decisions, and what is the real access-decision endpoint and grant model for pii:read?
Should ingestion-service parse the `tags:` comment convention, or forward the raw comment and let metadata-graph parse it? This plan assumes ingestion-service parses and forwards tags.
What is the tag-to-classification mapping beyond `pii` -> PII (e.g. do `email`, `ssn`, `phone` alone imply PII; do `confidential`/`internal`/`public` tags map directly)?
What classification applies to columns with no tags and no steward value: null/unclassified (this plan's assumption, not masked) or a default such as INTERNAL?
Should CONFIDENTIAL columns also be masked for some requesters, or is masking limited to PII per acceptance criterion 3?
Should masking fail closed (mask when the access decision or classification is unavailable) or fail open during rollout?
What masking format is required per data type (null, fixed token, partial e.g. j***@example.com, hash) and must it be type-preserving?
Which PII-format rules apply (email, phone, SSN, ...) and how is the rule chosen: from tags like `email`, or from a separate PII subtype on the column?
Is there an audit requirement for who changed a classification and when (affects the override endpoint and storage)?
Is dq.result.published.v1 expected to carry per-rule results for PII rules, which would make it a contract change?
Does platform-sdk depend on platform-contracts (generated models), which would fix the release order between them?
